Deutsche Bank's 2027 Question: Can Record Earnings Survive a Tougher Funding Climate?
sum: Deutsche Bank investors are being forced to weigh two competing narratives, and the tension between them has little to do with any single trading session. On one side sits the most profitable quarter the bank has ever posted. On the other, a gathering set of worries about what happens once the current cycle turns — specifically, whether the improved earnings power holds up through 2027.

The stock has been caught in the crossfire. It fell 3.5% in one session and 2.9% in another, both moves set against a broad selloff in European equities. The second decline came amid a global AI-driven retreat, with Reuters reporting concerns over potential restrictions on AI data centers, stretched valuations and debt-financed investment. Against that tape, company-specific progress struggles to register.

Roughly a week ago, Deutsche Bank lifted its full-year 2026 revenue guidance to more than EUR 33 billion. The cost target stayed put at around EUR 21.3 billion. That pairing is the real test: higher revenue has to materialize without the expense line creeping up to meet it. Judging the top line in isolation would miss the second half of the equation entirely.

The third-quarter report offers a starting point. Pre-tax profit for Q3 2026 rose 8% to EUR 2.6 billion, and net profit hit a record EUR 1.9 billion. Those figures, released about two weeks ago, underpin confidence in the bank's earning power — provided it can build on them.

Analysts currently expect earnings per share of EUR 3.31 for 2026, a concrete anchor for valuation. A dividend of EUR 1.16 per share is forecast for 2026, up from EUR 1.00 for 2025. That payout only strengthens the investment case if profits can carry it.

Goldman Sachs added its voice on Tuesday. According to media reports, the firm raised its price target to EUR 47.75 from EUR 44.25 while reaffirming its buy rating. Analyst Chris Hallam adjusted his estimates to reflect the quarterly report and described an "era of higher profitability." The stock also earned a place on Goldman's European list of particularly convincing investment ideas.
The direction of the estimate revision matters more than the target itself.

items.t: Deutsche Bank Upgrades JetBlue to Buy and Raises Target to $5.50
sum: Deutsche Bank upgraded JetBlue Airways to Buy from Hold on Thursday and lifted its price target to $5.50 from $3, citing a more favorable airline backdrop and planned product launches. The new target implies 54% upside to Wednesday’s close.

Deutsche Bank analyst Michael Linenberg said an industry focus on “yield in response to inflationary pressures,” including higher fuel prices, may disproportionately benefit airlines serving value-conscious, discretionary travelers. He also expects planned product launches at JetBlue and Frontier to support revenue and margins from 2027 onward.
The bank also cited positive airline returns in 21 of the last 25 years’ December quarters. The upgrade differed from the broader analyst view: 13 of 18 analysts covering JetBlue had Hold ratings.

JetBlue shares had gained more than 16% over the week through Thursday, following the airline’s Oct. 26 increase to its full-year revenue per available seat mile guidance. The stock remained down about 22% year to date as higher fuel costs tied to the Iran war pressured margins. JetBlue’s third-quarter results included a $257 million loss as its fuel bill rose 61%.

Deutsche Bank (XTRA:DBK) Returns To Debt Markets, Is The Stock Fully Priced?
sum: Deutsche Bank (XTRA:DBK) has returned to the primary debt market with new 6.45% senior unsecured funding notes due November 2036. This fresh fixed income issuance gives equity investors another reference point on the bank's funding costs.

Recent trading has turned sharply positive for Deutsche Bank, with a 1-day share price return of 6.88% and a 7-day share price gain of 8.44% lifting the stock to €32.555. This comes even though the 90-day share price return is slightly down 0.52% and the year-to-date share price return is down 2.99%, while total shareholder return sits at 6.68% over 1 year. The very large 3-year and 5-year total shareholder return of about 2.4x suggests that today's bond issuance is being added to an already significantly changed equity story.

Scan other banks with active funding programs and similar equity re-ratings by checking our hand picked list of solid balance sheet and fundamentals (197 results) for comparison alongside Deutsche Bank.

After Deutsche Bank's sharp move to €32.555, the real tension is timing. Is this the moment to lean into the re rated story, or does waiting for a cooler entry make more sense once the valuation is on the table?

On the most widely followed narrative, Deutsche Bank is pinned at a fair value of €32.40, almost identical to the last close at €32.56, which leaves the argument less about discount and more about whether the current mix of profitability and capital returns holds together.

Conclusão: O Q1 2026 confirma que o Deutsche Bank não é mais uma história de "reestruturação", mas sim de execução e crescimento. A sólida geração orgânica de capital e o foco em eficiência operacional colocam a ação em uma posição favorável para investidores que buscam exposição ao setor bancário europeu com foco em retorno de capital.
Still, Deutsche Bank's fair value hinges on execution, and setbacks in credit quality or a weaker German economy could quickly challenge this newly re-rated story.

Deutsche Bank stock awaits London IPO revival after Numis deal
sum: Deutsche Bank's London investment-banking strategy is still waiting for a revival in initial public offerings, according to a Bloomberg report published on Wednesday, November 4, 2026. The report examines the progress of the bank's UK corporate-broker business three years after the Numis acquisition.

Deutsche Bank bought London-based corporate broker Numis in spring 2023, when market conditions appeared to be improving. The bank expected access to more than 160 Numis clients and hoped to win additional mandates from companies seeking listings on the London Stock Exchange.

That anticipated flow of transactions has not materialized. Bloomberg reports that initial public offerings have remained few and far between, leaving the strategic payoff from the acquisition dependent on a broader recovery in London's equity-capital-markets activity.

With the IPO market still subdued, Deutsche Bank has focused more heavily on larger British corporates. The lender is also seeking to sell additional banking services to existing Numis clients, broadening the commercial relationship beyond the original corporate-broker mandate.

The development matters for investors because the Numis deal was intended to strengthen Deutsche Bank's access to UK companies and potential capital-markets business. A prolonged shortage of listings limits the most visible source of growth, while the broader corporate approach may offer another route to building revenue from the acquired client base.

Volkswagen Keeps Deutsche Bank's Buy Rating Despite Trimmed Target as China Slide and Porsche Writed
sum: Deutsche Bank has trimmed its price target on Volkswagen's preference shares from EUR 105 to EUR 100 while leaving its buy recommendation in place, a two-speed signal that separates the bank from JPMorgan's more guarded stance on the embattled automaker.

Analyst Tim Rokossa cut the target following a sit-down with VW finance chief Arno Antlitz, an exchange he described as constructive. Talks centered on the ongoing restructuring, cost reduction in Germany and the worsening situation in China. The lower target nonetheless shows that even a positive read on management's plans was not enough to justify an unchanged valuation. The stock added 0.6% in the prior session.

JPMorgan had already moved on Friday, slashing its target from EUR 110 to EUR 85 after the quarterly figures while reaffirming a neutral rating. Media reports pointed to heavy one-off and write-down effects in the most recent quarter as the trigger. Both houses are marking down their valuation expectations; they part ways on what investors should do about it. A reduced target does not amount to a sell call — Deutsche Bank's underlying view stays positive, whereas JPMorgan remains on the sidelines.

The weaker earnings base explains the caution. Volkswagen booked a net loss after tax of EUR 5.8 billion for the third quarter of 2026, dragged down in large part by a non-cash Porsche goodwill impairment of EUR 6.4 billion. That figure cannot be read simply as a verdict on day-to-day operations — but neither does the write-down excuse the operating problems. Earnings power at the core Volkswagen brand remains the key test of the overhaul.

For the first nine months of 2026, the group reported operating profit of EUR 71 million, down from EUR 5,408 million a year earlier. Before special items, operating profit reached EUR 8.8 billion. Management stressed the immediate need for action in light of the nine-month balance sheet. For the full year, Volkswagen expects revenue of around EUR 315 billion and an operating return on sales of up to 1%.
At the brand level, Volkswagen Pkw generated operating profit of EUR 813 million from January to September 2026, a 1.3% operating margin that leaves limited financial headroom.

CrowdStrike Slides 3% Despite Deutsche Bank Upgrade and CoreWeave Deal; Fortinet Falls 3%, Palo Alto Drops 2%
sum: A Deutsche Bank upgrade and a major AI infrastructure deal handed CrowdStrike two reasons to rally, yet the stock still fell. What that tells investors about the broader cybersecurity selloff is worth a closer look.

Two bullish headlines couldn’t keep CrowdStrike Holdings (NASDAQ:CRWD | CRWD Price Prediction) from slipping as cybersecurity stocks sold off to open the week. CrowdStrike stock is at $242.58, down 3% early in the session. Early gains tied to the upgrade news faded once the opening bell rang, extending a decline from the prior session.

Expectations were already elevated for CrowdStrike before the latest news arrived. Shares of the company are up 107% year to date (YTD), and a run that large can invite profit taking even on good news. Rotation within tech has picked up after a rough stretch for AI-linked stocks and heavy scrutiny of AI spending, making sector rotation another possible force behind the selling.

Deutsche Bank analyst Brad Zelnick upgraded CrowdStrike to Buy from Hold on November 2 and raised his price target to $300 from $240. Zelnick argued that investors underappreciate how much AI could expand the cybersecurity market, citing a “tsunami of cyber demand materializing as the AI frontier advances.” In his view, CrowdStrike’s own estimate of a $565 billion total addressable market by 2034 could prove conservative.

On the same day, CrowdStrike expanded its partnership with CoreWeave (NASDAQ:CRWV), giving CoreWeave customers access to the Falcon platform and round-the-clock managed security. Chief Business Officer Daniel Bernard explained the logic for CrowdStrike simply: “Production AI is becoming mission-critical, and adversaries know it.” For CrowdStrike, the deal expands its reach into AI infrastructure, a market management has highlighted as a major growth opportunity.

Both announcements build on CrowdStrike’s strong August 26 earnings report. Revenue at CrowdStrike rose 25.8% year over year (YoY) to $1.47 billion in Q2 FY2027, while net new annual recurring revenue (ARR) jumped 51% to $332.8 million. CrowdStrike also disclosed that Falcon Flex ending ARR topped $2.29 billion, up 101%, and it raised its full-year guidance.

Aixtron's Upgrades Cut Both Ways as Chip Selloff Drowns Out a Doubling Order Book
sum: Aixtron spent the week proving that a strong order book and a rising share price are two very different things. The German deposition-equipment maker watched its stock slide as a global semiconductor selloff swept through European chip names, with the day's move put at -4.4% in the latest reading — deepening from the -3.8% recorded a session earlier — as disappointing quarterly reports and cautious guidance from Amazon and Intel dragged the whole technology complex lower.

The retreat had nothing to do with anything Aixtron itself reported. Both accounts attribute the weakness squarely to the sector backdrop, not to any fresh negative company disclosure. What makes the episode worth unpacking is the collision it sets up: company-specific signals are improving at precisely the moment investors are re-pricing sector risk.

Deutsche Bank Research upgraded the stock from "Hold" to "Buy" — while trimming its price target to EUR 42 from EUR 44. Analyst Michael Kuhn pointed to continued positive momentum in equipment for optoelectronic chips and an earlier-than-expected recovery in power semiconductors. A better rating paired with a lower target is an unusual combination, and it frames the debate neatly: the demand picture is brightening, but the number attached to it came down.

The DZ Bank moved the other way on valuation. Analyst Armin Kremser cut his fair value to EUR 37.50 from EUR 40.00 and kept a "Hold" rating, flagging the production ramp and supply-chain assurance as live risks. Jefferies, for its part, reaffirmed its Buy recommendation with a EUR 44 target; analyst Om Bakhda highlighted accelerating order momentum in equipment for silicon carbide and gallium nitride chips.

Read together, the three opinions mark out two separate checkpoints for investors — the strength of demand on one side, the ability to execute on the other. Optimism about new orders does not erase operational reservations, and no analyst note substitutes for future results.

The concrete anchor for the bullish case landed on Thursday: Aixtron reported third-quarter 2026 order intake of EUR 274.9 million, up 122% year on year. Management credited the surge mainly to tools for laser applications in AI data-center communications. The equipment order backlog stood at EUR 549.4 million.

PDD Holdings Rose as Deutsche Bank Upgraded It to Buy. Here’s Where the Stock Could Go by 2030
sum: PDD Holdings (PDD) rose 2.34% to $79.28 on October 29 after Deutsche Bank upgraded the stock to Buy from Hold, while Alibaba slipped 1.41% the same session. Deutsche kept its $105 price target, so the upgrade rests on the lower share price. Three days earlier, the European Commission accepted Temu’s plan to fix a Digital Services Act breach that drew a €200 million fine in May. The shares are still down 30% in 2026.

Deutsche Bank analyst Peter Milliken set the $105 target on August 24, when PDD closed at $87.07, and kept it with the upgrade. He said the valuation is “too attractive for us to look past,” while also calling Street consensus optimistic, according to TheFly. The target sits about 32% above the October 29 close and below the Street’s mean of around $115. JPMorgan is more cautious: it cut its target to $95 on September 10 and rates the stock Neutral.

His consensus warning fits the record. PDD has missed the Street’s revenue estimate four quarters in a row, by 0.42% to 2.90%. Second-quarter revenue of CN¥112.36 billion came in 1.36% short, even as adjusted EPS of CN¥19.33 beat TIKR’s consensus by 5.34%.

On the August 24 call, Co-Chairman and Co-CEO Zhao Jiazhen said PDD had significantly raised R&D spending on platform governance. He said the platform had introduced more than 150 trust and safety measures to date and launched over 50 targeted initiatives in June alone. Financial Director Jun Liu put non-GAAP R&D at RMB 4.3 billion, up 40%, with non-GAAP operating expenses at 31% of revenue versus 29% a year earlier.
Co-Chairman and Co-CEO Chen Lei pointed to rules abroad: “Since the beginning of the year, global regulatory and compliance landscapes have undergone a significant shift.”

Temu’s EU case is one of those rules in motion. The Commission accepted a plan with five measures and gave Temu four months to conduct an interim risk assessment. It is an accepted plan, not a closed case, and management has not linked the R&D increase to it. Temu also still faces the EU’s €3 charge on low-value parcels, in place since July. Zhao added that the first-party brand rollout has taken longer than originally expected.
TIKR tracks 37 analysts on PDD Holdings. How many say “Buy”?

Deutsche Bank lifts target for JD Sports stock to GBp 105
sum: JD Sports Fashion (ISIN GB00BM8Q5M07) received a higher Deutsche Bank target on October 28, 2026, from GBp 95 to GBp 105, while the bank retained its Hold rating, according to Proactive Investors. The revised target gives the retailer a concrete valuation reference, but the unchanged rating keeps the earnings outlook central to the debate.

JD's North American operation accounted for 38 percent of group organic sales in fiscal 2026 and had more than 2,500 stores across five complementary fascias. The company presented those figures during a two-day investor and analyst visit to Florida, described in its October 19, 2026 release by JD Sports Fashion.

The regional platform includes JD, Finish Line at Macy's, DTLR, Shoe Palace and Hibbett. Hibbett alone operated 965 stores across 36 states, giving the group a broad route into US communities while the JD fascia continued building its own brand presence.

The investment case rests on infrastructure as much as store count. JD said it invested USD 362 million in new stores and its existing estate from fiscal 2023 through fiscal 2026, alongside USD 100 million in supply-chain capital spending and USD 42 million in digital and technology capital spending, according to the same company release.

The company also said its North American JD fascia had more than 450 stores. That combination of physical reach and technology spending provides the operating context for Deutsche Bank's constructive comments on sales and margins, even as its Hold rating signals that improved visibility is still required.

Senior Independent Director Kath Smith will leave JD's board on January 19, 2027, after more than seven years with the group, according to the company's regulatory announcement. The change is separate from the target revision but adds a defined governance date for shareholders.

JD Sports Fashion was trading at EUR 1.12 at Lang & Schwarz on October 29, 2026 at 1:06 p.m. CEST. The primary listing is on the London Stock Exchange, where the share was quoted at GBp 92.86 at 12:10 p.m. GMT on October 29, 2026.

Deutsche Bank shares up as Q3 profit beats forecasts on record inflows
sum: Investing.com -- Deutsche Bank shares rose more than 3% on Wednesday after Germany's largest lender beat third-quarter profit forecasts, with record inflows into wealth and asset management and flat costs outweighing higher loan-loss provisions.
Pretax profit came in at €2.63 billion, about 10% above the €2.39 billion expected in a company-compiled consensus and up 8% from a year earlier.
Profit after tax was €1.9 billion, a record for a third consecutive quarter, against consensus of €1.7 billion.

Net revenues rose 4% to €8.3 billion, ahead of the €8.2 billion consensus. Diluted earnings per share were €0.94, versus €0.77 expected. Post-tax return on tangible equity was 10.6%, compared with 9.9% expected.

Noninterest expenses were flat year on year at €5.2 billion, below the €5.33 billion consensus, as €0.3 billion of incremental investment was largely offset by €0.2 billion of efficiencies. The cost/income ratio improved to 62.4% from 64.4%, versus 65.0% expected.

Asset-gathering businesses attracted record inflows. Asset Management took in €31 billion, its second consecutive record quarter, driven by passive products, lifting assets under management above €1.2 trillion.

Private Bank, which houses Wealth Management, recorded net inflows of €17 billion, a record, with client assets at €865 billion; Wealth Management revenues rose 10%. Group assets under management rose €50 billion in the quarter to €2.0 trillion on record net inflows of €47 billion.

Analyst Liam Fitzpatrick cut his price target to 3,300p from 3,600p following the miner's third-quarter production report, against a latest closing share price of 3,174p.
The shares have underperformed copper and listed mining peers by around 5% to 15% over the past month, creating scope for a reassessment as investors absorb the revised targets.

Antofagasta has missed its production guidance every year since 2021, undermining investor confidence in its ability to deliver against published targets.

- Deutsche has a 'Hold' rating and a $34 price target on SEDG.

Shares of SolarEdge Technologies (SEDG) fell on Wednesday after Deutsche Bank labeled the stock a short-term sell idea, citing softer U.S. demand and risk to later-year earnings.
The shares were down about 5% at the time of writing, trading near $32.30.

The decline followed a research note from Deutsche Bank analyst Corinne Blanchard, who placed a "Catalyst Call: Sell" on SolarEdge as a short-term investment idea. The firm kept a 'Hold' rating and a $34 price target. Blanchard wrote that core revenue growth in coming quarters is likely to run softer than expected because of U.S. market conditions, though European trends, particularly in storage, could offset part of that weakness.

She said elevated interest rates are weighing on U.S. demand and sees risk to fourth-quarter and 2027 earnings. Deutsche Bank's fourth-quarter 2026 revenue estimate sits about 2% below consensus, and its 2027 revenue projection is about 5% below. Blanchard pointed to the company's third-quarter report, expected around Nov. 4, and the RE+ conference on Nov. 16–19 as points where guidance and industry commentary could reset expectations.

Nvidia Nears $6T Record as Deutsche Bank Warns Stocks and Bonds Cannot Both Be Right
sum: Nvidia is trading at record highs Tuesday, pushing its market capitalization to within roughly $200 billion of a $6 trillion milestone no company has ever crossed — and doing so precisely as the US bond market sends a macro warning signal that has not been this loud in nearly a quarter century. Deutsche Bank's research team has issued a direct challenge to the current equity rally: bonds and stocks are pricing two irreconcilable worlds, and one of them will have to yield.

Shares of the Santa Clara, California-based chipmaker have gained approximately 28% in 2026, adding more than $1.2 trillion to Nvidia's market value along the way. The rally has been relentless enough that the company is now closing in on a threshold that would have seemed unimaginable even 18 months ago: the first $6 trillion market capitalization in the history of publicly traded companies. At that level, Nvidia would be worth more than Amazon, Meta Platforms, Tesla, and Netflix combined.

The company's ascent from $1 trillion in June 2023 to the current approximately $5.8 trillion has been the fastest wealth creation run in stock market history, driven by an AI infrastructure boom that shows no structural signs of abating. Nvidia's share of the S&P 500 index has grown accordingly — the chipmaker now represents approximately 7 to 8% of the index, meaning its performance is directly embedded in the retirement portfolios of millions of Americans who have never bought a single share of NVDA.

A key accelerant for the October 2026 rally was a $150 billion increase to Nvidia's share repurchase authorization, announced September 28 — the largest single buyback in US corporate history. With the new authorization, Nvidia's total remaining repurchase capacity stands at $235 billion. CEO Jensen Huang described the backdrop as a "once-in-a-generation platform shift to AI and accelerated computing" and said the company planned to double chip shipments in 2027 as data center construction accelerates.

The specific reason Nvidia can sustain the valuation its stock reflects is a structural economic advantage that goes well beyond chip performance. When a hyperscaler — Amazon, Google, Microsoft, Meta — builds an AI training cluster, it is not simply buying graphics processing units.

According to finanzen.ch, Deutsche Bank shares were up 0.2 percent at 33.69 EUR in Xetra at 12:28 p.m. CET on September 17, 2026, after starting the trading day at 33.64 EUR and touching an intraday high of 33.80 EUR.
The same overview from finanzen.ch states that Deutsche Bank stock reached its 52-week high at 35.85 EUR on September 8, 2026 and marked a 52-week low at 23.82 EUR on March 23, 2026.

Based on these figures, the price of 33.69 EUR on September 17, 2026 was 6.41 percent below the 52-week high of 35.85 EUR, while the 52-week low of 23.82 EUR lies 29.30 percent beneath the then current level, illustrating both the recovery since March and the remaining upside to the early-September peak.

The same price report from finanzen.ch highlights that analyst estimates point to earnings of 3.34 EUR per share for Deutsche Bank in fiscal year 2026, providing a benchmark for investors assessing the valuation of the stock at current levels.

With a share price around 33.69 EUR on September 17, 2026 and a 2026 earnings-per-share estimate of 3.34 EUR, the implied price-earnings ratio stands close to 10.1, a level that many investors view as moderate for a major European bank given the group’s restructuring progress and remaining regulatory and macroeconomic risks.

For comparison, the 52-week low of 23.82 EUR recorded on March 23, 2026 would correspond to a price-earnings ratio of roughly 7.1 on the same 2026 EPS estimate of 3.34 EUR, underlining how strongly market confidence and risk appetite have improved over the course of 2026 as the share price moved away from that trough.

ATOSS stock gains on Deutsche Bank price target hike and solid half-year figures
sum: ATOSS Software SE stock (ISIN DE0005104400) closed at 90.90 EUR on Xetra on September 16, 2026, up 0.55% from the prior close of 90.40 EUR, and remains well supported between its 52-week low and high. According to Ad-hoc-news, Deutsche Bank Research raised its price target for ATOSS stock to 115 EUR on September 4, 2026, while keeping a Buy rating, giving investors a fresh reference point for the workforce management specialist.

As Ad-hoc-news reports, Deutsche Bank Research adjusted its view on ATOSS Software on September 4, 2026, increasing the price target from a previously lower level to 115 EUR and reiterating a Buy recommendation. With the shares closing at 90.90 EUR as of September 16, 2026, this implies a gap of 24.10 EUR or around 26.5% between the current Xetra level and the bank’s target, highlighting potential upside if the company can sustain its growth trajectory.

The same overview cited by Ad-hoc-news points out that ATOSS stock is trading between its 12-month low and high, with the latest small caps data indicating a 52-week low of 65.00 EUR and a 52-week high of 124.00 EUR on Xetra. At the September 16, 2026 close of 90.90 EUR, the shares therefore stand 25.90 EUR above the 52-week low and 33.10 EUR below the 52-week high, underlining that the current price sits roughly mid-range in the recent trading corridor rather than at an extreme.

According to Ad-hoc-news, ATOSS delivered strong half-year 2026 results that helped justify the positive analyst stance. In the first half of 2026 the company increased its revenue to a level that was clearly above the comparable period of the previous year, with double-digit percentage growth driven by continued demand for workforce management and cloud-based solutions. The same report notes that operating profitability remained robust, as ATOSS was able to keep its margins healthy while expanding its top line, a combination that tends to be valued highly in the software sector.

As summarized by Ad-hoc-news, management also confirmed its guidance for the 2026 financial year in the wake of the half-year figures, signaling confidence that the current growth momentum in workforce management software can be sustained.

Deutsche Bank downgrades Softcat, upgrades Bytes Technology
sum: Deutsche Bank downgraded Softcat but upgraded Bytes Technology on Wednesday as it took a look at the UK software and IT services sector.
DB noted that the sector has performed strongly in the last three months and is now slightly above where it was at the start of the year and around 42% above the low it hit in late March.

"Whilst a lot of this performance was accounted for by Computacenter, Softcat and Kainos which had upgrades, there has also been improved investor sentiment more recently, reflecting the swinging perception of the risk posed by AI on what are seen as traditional business models for Software and IT services," it said.
The bank cut Softcat to ‘hold’ from ‘buy’ but lifted the price target to 2,140p from 1,800p. It upgraded Bytes to ‘buy’ from ‘hold’ and increased the price target to 500p from 410p.
Deutsche lifted its stance on Cerillion to ‘buy’ from ‘hold’ but cut the price target to 1,400p from 1,575p.
At 1038 BST, Softcat shares were down 2.2% at 2,036p, while Bytes was 3% higher at 426p. Cerillion shares were 0.8% lower at 960p.

Deutsche Bank stock starts €500 million buyback as shares trade close to recent highs
sum: Deutsche Bank AG (ISIN DE0005140008) stock is seeing renewed investor attention on August 25, 2026, as the group launches a new €500 million share buyback program while its shares trade close to recent 52-week highs after solid profit generation in the latest reported fiscal year, according to recent market data and company disclosures. This combination of capital return and resilient earnings provides a fresh catalyst for the stock and frames the risk-reward picture for holders of the Frankfurt-listed shares.

Per a detailed valuation overview published on August 24, 2026, Deutsche Bank announced a €500 million share repurchase program funded by this year’s net profits and supported by existing capital deductions, with the buyback set to begin on August 25, 2026. This capital return package follows a period of steady profitability that has enabled the bank to commit cash to shareholders while maintaining regulatory capital buffers, underscoring management’s confidence in the earnings outlook for the current year. The same analysis highlights that the stock trades on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker DB, where it was recently priced at $38.54, very close to its stated 52-week high of $40.43, illustrating that the shares have been on a strong run into the buyback start date.

That market snapshot also notes an estimated intrinsic value per Deutsche Bank share of $25.18 based on a proprietary valuation model, which sits $13.36 below the referenced market price of $38.54 and implies that the stock is valued 53.1 percent above that intrinsic estimate. For investors, this quantified gap between the trading level and model-based fair value introduces a clear valuation debate: on one side, the buyback and profitability support the case for the higher price, while on the other side, the model suggests that the shares may already reflect a substantial earnings and capital-return premium relative to historical norms.

On the home market in Frankfurt, intraday Xetra data for August 25, 2026, show Deutsche Bank shares trading in a relatively tight range while still benefiting from the announced buyback. At midday, an equity quote overview reported the stock at EUR 33.28, which was up 0.7 percent from the opening level of EUR 33.06 recorded earlier in the session.

Porvair shares rise after Deutsche Bank starts coverage with Buy rating (PRV)
sum: Shares in Porvair PLC (LSE:PRV) moved higher on Tuesday after Deutsche Bank initiated coverage of the industrial technology group with a Buy recommendation, citing the company's resilient business model, recurring revenue streams and long-term earnings growth potential.
Porvair's shares gained almost 2% to 834 pence in London trading, outperforming the FTSE 100, which was up around 0.3%.

Deutsche Bank assigned the stock a price target of 1,050 pence, implying significant upside from Monday's closing price of 818 pence. The broker described Porvair as a high-quality industrial business specialising in filtration, laboratory equipment and metal melt technologies, serving a broad range of mission-critical applications across multiple industries.

According to Deutsche Bank, many of the company's products are integrated into customers' manufacturing and testing processes, generating recurring demand through consumable sales, maintenance requirements and replacement cycles. The broker also highlighted strict regulatory standards and product certification requirements as key barriers to entry that help support long-term recurring revenue.

The research note added that Porvair's decentralised operating structure and well-established acquisition strategy have enabled the company to expand its technology portfolio while consistently growing earnings through disciplined acquisitions.

Deutsche Bank noted that Porvair has delivered compound annual earnings per share growth of around 15% over the past 15 years, significantly outperforming the wider UK engineering sector. The only year in which earnings declined was during the COVID-19 pandemic.

Looking ahead, the broker expects Porvair to continue delivering long-term earnings growth, supported by resilient end markets, disciplined margin management and further acquisition opportunities, reinforcing its positive investment case within the European industrial sector.

items.t: Bayer shares soar in Frankfurt; analysts are optimistic following the landmark ruling by the US Supreme Court
sum: Deutsche Bank has upgraded its recommendation to “buy”, following the ruling in the company’s favour in the billion-dollar glyphosate lawsuits relating to the herbicide’s alleged carcinogenicity

(Il Sole 24 Ore Radiocor) - Bayer is leading the way on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange, thanks to positive comments from Deutsche Bank analysts and also to the decision to set up a separate entity dedicated to the US operations of the controversial herbicide glyphosate. Shares in the German pharmaceutical and agrochemical giant rose by around 5 per cent, putting it in first place among the components of the DAX index. The share price climbed to €51.80, its highest level since August 2023.

Analysts at Deutsche Bank have upgraded their recommendation on the share to ‘buy’ from ‘hold’ and raised the target price from 45 to 60 euros, following the landmark ruling by the US Supreme Court in favour of Bayer concerning the multi-billion-euro glyphosate lawsuits relating to the herbicide’s alleged carcinogenicity.

DB’s experts believe that the group is now on a positive trajectory and that the focus should gradually shift to the fundamentals and growth prospects of the Crop and Pharma sectors. The German group has also announced its intention to consolidate its US herbicide-related activities into a dedicated subsidiary.

The spin-off forms part of the five-year programme to streamline operations presented last year for the Crop Science agricultural division, Bayer explained. The new company is called Ruveon and includes the production of Roundup, the brand name under which the glyphosate-based herbicide is marketed. Based in St Louis, Missouri, Ruveon will supply the US agricultural sector with “essential glyphosate-based products, meeting the highest standards of quality and service”, according to a press release. Ruveon remains a subsidiary of the Bayer Group.

The US Supreme Court has ruled in favour of Bayer regarding allegations of ‘failure to provide information’ concerning the labelling of glyphosate, which form the basis of the majority of the litigation. Although this ruling does not eliminate all legal risks, industry observers believe it will significantly reduce out-of-court settlements relating to Roundup cases.

sum: Stock market today: The Indian stock market closed in negative territory on Tuesday, 30 June, with the benchmark Nifty 50 slipping below the 23,900 mark. The Sensex fell 249.70 points, or 0.33%, to end at 76,478.67, while the Nifty 50 declined 80.50 points, or 0.34%, to settle at 23,865.75.

However, the market is likely to open flat as trends in the Gift Nifty index signalled a muted start on Wednesday, 1 July. Gift Nifty was trading near the 23,994 mark, down over 16 points from the previous close of Nifty futures.

"The broader market is expected to trade with a cautious undertone. Supportive global cues, including gains on Wall Street overnight and a positive trend across Asian equities in early trade, are likely to underpin sentiment at the open.

However, investors are expected to remain cautious at higher levels as uncertainty continues to surround the ongoing US–Iran negotiations in Doha. Market participants are closely tracking the second round of talks involving U.S. envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, while Iran's continued insistence on full control over the Strait of Hormuz highlights unresolved differences over the proposed ceasefire framework. As a result, headline-driven volatility is likely to persist until greater clarity emerges on the diplomatic front," said Ponmudi R, CEO of Enrich Money.
As the market is pointing towards a negative start, some stocks are likely to remain in focus on Wednesday due to their own positive/negative triggers.
HDFC Bank is set to appoint Jigar Shah as its General Counsel. Shah currently serves as Managing Director and Head of Compliance at the Indian subsidiary of global private equity firm KKR.

Kotak Mahindra Bank on Tuesday announced that it will acquire the retail banking, private banking, and wealth management businesses of Deutsche Bank in India for around ₹282 crore ($29.79 million), marking the German lender's exit from the country's retail banking segment.
